name: A Spanish-speaking AI DJ, requested into existence
object: AI DJ's Spanish-language voice and curation, launching for Spanish-speaking Premium listeners
audience: Spanish-speaking Spotify users who had been asking for AI DJ in their own language
message: This video tells Spanish-speaking listeners that the AI DJ feature they asked for now speaks their language and curates a session built entirely around their own listening history.

moments.what: A screenshotted fan reply to Spotify's Mexico account asks when AI DJ is coming to Mexico; the screen cuts to a blue card with a spinning green ring logo and bold type revealing the answer.
moments.copy: pa cuando el AI DJ en México? / tu nueva DJ personal.

moments.what: Large kinetic type explains the feature over blue and black cards, alongside a small 'DJ (beta)' app icon.
moments.copy: Mezclando lo mejor de tu Spotify en una sesión musical, creada solo para ti.

moments.what: A run of bold-type cards, each paired with a tilted phone mockup playing a track, walks through how the session is built: old favourites, mood-matched picks, liked songs, then new discoveries.
moments.copy: Desde la música que te transporta al pasado hasta hits que encienden el fin de semana... empezamos con artistas que escuchaste sin parar, seguimos con lo que te gusta, y descubrimos temas nuevos que suenan a ti.

moments.what: Type builds to 'experiencia musical', then a phone screenshot shows someone typing 'DJ' into the search bar, followed by a plain instruction card and the Spotify logo.
moments.copy: Solo busca DJ, dale click y listo. Pruébalo ahora.

cta: A plain instruction card, 'just search DJ, tap it, done,' paired with a search-bar screenshot, closing on 'Try it now' and the Spotify logo.
why: Opening on a real fan's own request to the brand (rather than a staged scenario) makes the localisation feel like a direct answer, and the all-text, all-motion treatment keeps the pace fast enough to explain the curation logic (past favourites, mood, new discoveries) in a minute without needing footage of a person at all. The CTA stays deliberately mundane — just search and tap — so the feature, not the ad, is what's being sold.
